subject: 🏃 Monday — Hip Complex Circuit (Wk 4)
html:
Tomorrow: 20-min Hip Complex Circuit — bodyweight mobility only, no running. Two rounds: foam roller T-spine extensions (8–10 reps), standing lunges with hip IR + extension (8–10 each side), quadruped banded hip IR (5–10 each side), 90/90 switches (8–10 each side), adductor rockbacks (8–10 reps), quadruped hip CARs (3 each direction, each leg), half-kneeling couch stretch (60 sec each side). This is the prescribed PT-heavy mobility flush — do it all, no time-crunch cuts.

PT block priority: The side plank with hip abduction (top toe down, 8 each side), dead bug with banded pulldown (2–3×10 slow marches), and chin tuck + lifts (2 reps each direction) got dropped on Friday for the second week running. Tack them onto the end of tomorrow's circuit — 5 extra minutes. These are Akanksha's prescriptions for the medial PFJ diagnosis, not optional accessories.

Focus cue: Sink into the hip internal rotation on the quadruped CARs and the standing lunges. PT flagged bilateral IR limitation as a primary driver — that's what these movements are treating. Slow, deliberate, no momentum.

Context: Week 4 of 12, Phase 1 — benchmark taper week. The PAL 10K is Saturday, five days out. This week's structure is designed to shed fatigue while keeping neural drive: Tuesday is the last quality session (6×1000m VO2), Wednesday is maintenance-light strength, Thursday is easy + strides, Friday is full rest, Saturday you race. Today's circuit opens the taper with active recovery — exactly where you want to be after yesterday's 10.5-mile long run.

Quick note on yesterday: 10.5 mi at 8:03 avg with a 6:58 closing kick is a strong fitness signal — first double-digit run since September and you handled it cleanly at knee 1/5. But the prescription was 8:45–9:15 aerobic time-on-feet, and 8:03 is closer to steady-state than easy. Also, the H10 got left at home, so we flew that workout blind on HR. Two items for the week: (1) H10 strap goes next to your race kit tonight — non-negotiable for Saturday's 10K, and (2) next long run (12 mi, Jun 7) gets an explicit HR cap at 155.

Tonight: Hydrate well, eat a normal dinner, get to bed by 10. Lay out the band and foam roller for the morning so the circuit is grab-and-go. Five days to race day — the taper starts now.
